tema: The five senses and their organs
objetivo: For the student to identify the five senses (sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch), the organ for each one (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin), and what we perceive with them, and understand that they let us know the world and warn us of danger.
hatsumon: How do you know a stove is hot without touching it?

turnos.utterance_formal: Good morning, everyone. Let's start quietly: close your eyes for a moment and tell me what you can hear in the classroom.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Alright, morning everybody. Let's start nice and quiet: close your eyes a sec and tell me what you can hear in here.

turnos.utterance_formal: Take out your notebooks; today we'll make a list with their organs.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Take out your notebooks; today we're gonna make a little list with their organs.

turnos.utterance_formal: Think about this: how do you know a stove is hot without even touching it?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Okay, think about it: how do you know a stove is hot without even touching it?

turnos.utterance_formal: Hold on to your answer; at the end we'll answer it completely.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Hold on to your answer; at the end we'll answer it all the way.

turnos.utterance_formal: Everything we know about the world reaches us through our body.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Everything we know about the world reaches us through our body.

operations.text: We get to know the world through our **body**.

turnos.utterance_formal: We call that way of perceiving what's around us a sense.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That way of perceiving what's around us, we call it a sense.

set.text: We get to know the world through our **body**. A **sense** is what lets us perceive what is around us.

turnos.utterance_formal: To perceive means to notice something. Let's go through them one by one.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: To perceive means to notice something. Let's go through them one by one.

turnos.utterance_formal: We have five senses, and each one works with an organ of the body.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: We have five senses, and each one works with an organ of the body.

set.text: We get to know the world through our **body**. A **sense** is what lets us perceive what is around us. We have five senses, and each one works with an organ.

turnos.utterance_formal: So today we're going to match up five senses with their five organs.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So today we're going to match up five senses with their five organs.

operations.text: Today we match 5 senses with their 5 **organs**.

turnos.utterance_formal: The first one is sight, and its organ is the eyes.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The first one is sight, and its organ is the eyes.

turnos.utterance_formal: With sight we notice colors, shapes, and light.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: With sight we notice colors, shapes, and light.

turnos.utterance_formal: Close your eyes for a second... see? Without them we can't perceive light.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Close your eyes for just a sec... see? Without them we can't perceive light.

operations.text: Without the eyes we can't perceive **light**.

turnos.utterance_formal: The eye works kind of like a camera that receives light.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The eye works kind of like a camera that receives light.

turnos.utterance_formal: The second one is hearing, and its organ is the ears.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The second one is hearing, and its organ is the ears.

turnos.utterance_formal: With hearing we perceive sounds, music, voices, and noises.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: With hearing we perceive so unds, music, voices, and noises.

turnos.utterance_formal: Sound enters through the ear, but the real hearing organ is on the inside.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Sound comes in through the ear, but the real deal is on the inside.

operations.text: Sound enters through the ear, but the real hearing **organ** is on the inside.

turnos.utterance_formal: So far we've covered two senses: sight and hearing.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So far we got two senses: sight and hearing.

turnos.utterance_formal: What we see on the outside is the ear; I'll leave one here as an example.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: What we see on the outside is the ear; I'll leave one here as an example.

turnos.utterance_formal: The third one is smell, and its organ is the nose.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The third one is smell, and its organ is the nose.

turnos.utterance_formal: With our nose we smell flowers, food, smoke, and perfume.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: With our nose we smell flowers, food, smoke, and per fume.

turnos.utterance_formal: Have you noticed that when you have a cold you can barely smell anything?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Have you noticed that when you have a cold you can barely smell anything?

operations.text: Smell fades when a cold blocks the nose.

turnos.utterance_formal: The fourth one is taste, and its organ is the tongue.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The fourth one is taste, and its organ is the tongue.

turnos.utterance_formal: With our tongue we tell apart sweet, salty, sour, and bitter.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: With our tongue we tell apart sweet, salty, so ur, and bitter.

turnos.utterance_formal: That's why we taste a lemon as sour and a piece of candy as sweet.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That's why we taste a lemon as sour and a piece of candy as sweet.

operations.text: A lemon tastes **sour** and candy tastes sweet.

turnos.utterance_formal: Look, we've written down four senses already: check out smell and taste.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Look, we got four senses written down already: check out smell and taste.

turnos.utterance_formal: And the fifth one is touch, whose organ is the skin.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And the fifth one is touch, whose organ is the skin.

turnos.utterance_formal: With our skin we feel cold, heat, smooth, rough, and pain.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: With our skin we feel cold, heat, smooth, ro ugh, and pain.

turnos.utterance_formal: Skin is special: it's not in just one place, it covers the whole body.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Skin is special: it's not in just one place, it covers the whole body.

turnos.utterance_formal: So skin is the biggest organ we have.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So skin is the biggest organ we have.

set.text: Skin covers the **whole body**. Skin is the biggest organ we have.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now all five senses are complete; look at them all together.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now all five senses are complete; look at them all together.

turnos.utterance_formal: Now, the senses aren't just for enjoying things; they also protect us.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now, the senses aren't just for enjoying stuff; they protect us too.

turnos.utterance_formal: The senses protect us: they warn us when there's danger nearby.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The senses protect us: they warn us when there's danger nearby.

turnos.utterance_formal: Go back to the stove thing: you feel the heat from far away and see the fire; they warn you before you get burned.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Go back to the stove thing: you feel the heat from far away and see the fire; they warn you before you get burned.

set.text: Senses warn us of **danger**. Feeling the heat from far away and seeing the fire warn us before we get burned.

turnos.utterance_formal: Smell warns us too: if something smells burnt, you need to be alert.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Smell warns us too: if something smells like it's burn ing, you gotta be alert.

operations.text: The smell of burning warns us of danger too.

turnos.utterance_formal: Has anyone's nose ever warned them that food was burning?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Has anyone's nose ever warned them that food was burning?

turnos.utterance_formal: And even pain is useful: it tells us something is hurting us.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And even pain is useful: it tells us something is hurting us.

set.text: The smell of burning warns us of danger too. Even **pain** is useful: it tells us something is hurting us.

turnos.utterance_formal: Go back and look at the question from the beginning: now we can answer it.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Go back and look at the question from the beginning: now we can answer it.

turnos.utterance_formal: So, how do you know the stove is hot without touching it? Your skin feels the heat from far away and your eyes see the fire.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So, how do you know the stove's hot without touchin' it? Well, your skin feels the heat from way over there and your eyes see the fire, right?

operations.text: Skin feels the **heat** and eyes see the fire, so we know the stove is hot without touching it.

turnos.utterance_formal: Rest your hand for a moment and then we'll wrap up with the important part.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Rest your hand a bit and then we'll wrap up with the important stuff.

turnos.utterance_formal: Hold on to today's big idea, the one that sums everything up.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Hold on to today's really big idea, the one that sums it all up.

set.text: Skin feels the **heat** and eyes see the fire, so we know the stove is hot without touching it. We have 5 **senses**, and each one has its own organ.

turnos.utterance_formal: And the pairing of each sense with its organ, don't mix them up.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And the pairing of each sense with its organ, don't get 'em mix ed up.

set.text: Skin feels the **heat** and eyes see the fire, so we know the stove is hot without touching it. We have 5 **senses**, and each one has its own organ. Sight is for the eyes, hearing for the ears, smell for the nose, taste for the tongue and touch for the skin.

turnos.utterance_formal: And today's big word, the one you shouldn't forget, is sense.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And today's big word, the one you shouldn't forget, is sense.

turnos.utterance_formal: Remember what a sense is: what lets us perceive what's around us.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Remember what a sense is: what lets us perceive what's around us.

turnos.utterance_formal: Very good, I can see it's clear. Excellent work.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Very good, I can see it's super clear. Excellent work.

turnos.utterance_formal: For homework, pick five things from your house and say which sense you perceive them with.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: For homework, pick five things from your house and say which sense you perceive them with.

operations.text: Pick five things from your house and say which sense you perceive each one with.

turnos.utterance_formal: And explain to me, for each sense, what danger it can protect you from.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And explain to me, for each sen se, what danger it can protect you from.

set.text: Pick five things from your house and say which sense you perceive each one with. Then explain what danger each sense protects you from.

turnos.utterance_formal: Does everyone have their homework written down? Very good.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Everybody got their homework written down? Alright, very good.

turnos.utterance_formal: Take one last look at the five senses we finished today.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Take one last look at the five senses we finished today.

turnos.utterance_formal: That's all for today. Pack up your things and I'll see you tomorrow.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That's it for today. Pack up your stuff and I'll see you tomorrow.
